content.text: No customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties, or minimum/early-termination fees appear anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, forfeiture or minimum-fee provision payable by Sparkling (the customer). Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay fees per the Fee Schedule; there is no late-payment interest or penalty. Section 17(b) permits Sparkling to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination fee or accelerated/remaining-term payment, and Section 17 default termination by Sparkling actually converts the licence to perpetual and requires Garman to refund prepaid fees for services not rendered. Sections 3, 9 and 19 impose no monetary penalties on Sparkling. Section 15 confirms each party's remedy is direct damages only, excluding consequential loss. Any LD-type amounts run in our favour, which the playbook treats as compliant, so no redline is required.
